arrow.q: Draw the curved-arrow mechanism for the SN2 reaction of hydroxide with bromomethane. Label nucleophile, electrophile and leaving group.
arrow.m: One arrow from an O lone pair of HO⁻ to the carbon of CH₃Br (forming the new O–C bond); one arrow from the C–Br bond to Br (Br⁻ leaves). A single concerted step with backside attack; product CH₃OH + Br⁻.

arrow.q: Draw the mechanism for protonation of an alkene by HBr followed by bromide capture, for propene.
arrow.m: Arrow 1: π bond of the alkene to the H of HBr (forming C–H on the terminal carbon); arrow 2: H–Br bond to Br (giving Br⁻). Intermediate: secondary carbocation CH₃CH⁺CH₃. Arrow 3: Br⁻ lone pair to the cation carbon. Product: 2-bromopropane.

arrow.q: Draw the E2 mechanism for 2-bromobutane with ethoxide giving 2-butene; show the required geometry.
arrow.m: One concerted step: ethoxide lone pair takes the β-H (on C3); the C–H bond electrons form the new C2=C3 π bond; the C–Br bond breaks with electrons to Br⁻. The H and Br must be anti-periplanar (dihedral 180°). Zaitsev product 2-butene (mostly trans).

arrow.q: Draw the mechanism for NaBH₄ reduction of cyclohexanone to cyclohexanol, including the workup.
arrow.m: Hydride (B–H bond electrons) attacks the carbonyl carbon; C=O π electrons move onto oxygen giving an alkoxide. Protonation of the alkoxide by the solvent (MeOH/H₃O⁺ workup) gives cyclohexanol.

arrow.q: Draw the acid-catalyzed hydrolysis mechanism of an ester RCOOR′ to a carboxylic acid and alcohol.
arrow.m: Protonate C=O; water attacks the carbonyl carbon; proton transfer to the OR′ oxygen; collapse of tetrahedral intermediate expels R′OH while re-forming C=O; deprotonate to give RCOOH. Every step is reversible; excess water drives it.

arrow.q: Draw the mechanism for nitration of benzene, including generation of the electrophile.
arrow.m: HNO₃ + H₂SO₄ → H₂O⁺–NO₂ → NO₂⁺ + H₂O (nitronium). π electrons of benzene attack N of NO₂⁺ giving the arenium (sigma) complex, with charge delocalized over ortho/para positions. HSO₄⁻ removes the ring H⁺ and the C–H electrons restore aromaticity to give nitrobenzene.

arrow.q: Draw the base-catalyzed aldol addition of acetaldehyde with itself, then dehydration to crotonaldehyde.
arrow.m: HO⁻ removes an α-H giving the enolate; the enolate carbon attacks the carbonyl carbon of a second aldehyde to give an alkoxide; protonation gives 3-hydroxybutanal. Heat/base: deprotonate the α-H, expel HO⁻ in E1cB to give CH₃CH=CHCHO.

arrow.q: Draw the Diels–Alder reaction of 1,3-butadiene with ethylene using arrows. Why is the diene required to be s-cis?
arrow.m: Three arrows in a cyclic flow: one π bond of the diene to form a new σ bond to the dienophile carbon, the dienophile π bond to form a σ bond to the other diene terminus, and the central C–C σ→π shift (diene central bond becomes a new π bond). Product: cyclohexene. s-cis needed so that both diene termini can reach the dienophile on the same face.

arrow.q: Draw the mechanism for the pinacol rearrangement of pinacol (2,3-dimethylbutane-2,3-diol) in acid.
arrow.m: Protonate one OH; loss of H₂O gives a tertiary carbocation; 1,2-methyl shift from the adjacent carbinol carbon (arrow from C–CH₃ bond to the cationic carbon) gives an oxocarbenium (protonated ketone); loss of H⁺ gives pinacolone (3,3-dimethyl-2-butanone).

arrow.q: Draw the mechanism of the Wittig reaction between Ph₃P=CH₂ and cyclohexanone.
arrow.m: Ylide carbon attacks the carbonyl carbon (and C=O π to O⁻) giving a betaine; formation of a four-membered oxaphosphetane (O⁻ attacks P⁺); retro-[2+2] gives methylenecyclohexane and Ph₃P=O (strong P=O bond is the driving force).

arrow.q: Draw the mechanism for the Baeyer–Villiger oxidation of cyclohexanone with mCPBA and say which group migrates in an unsymmetrical ketone.
arrow.m: Protonated ketone is attacked by the peracid to give the Criegee intermediate; the migrating group shifts to oxygen in a concerted step as carboxylate leaves; gives caprolactone for cyclohexanone. In unsymmetrical ketones the more electron-rich/substituted group migrates (tert-alkyl > sec-alkyl > aryl > primary > methyl).

arrow.q: Draw the catalytic cycle for a Suzuki coupling of Ar–Br with Ar′–B(OH)₂.
arrow.m: Pd(0)L₂ → oxidative addition of Ar–Br → ArPd(II)(Br)L₂ → base-assisted transmetalation with Ar′B(OH)₃⁻ gives ArPd(II)Ar′L₂ → reductive elimination forms Ar–Ar′ and regenerates Pd(0).

spectra.q: C₃H₆O: IR 1715 cm⁻¹ (strong); ¹H NMR δ 2.17 (s, 6H). Identify the compound.
spectra.m: Acetone. DBE = 1 (C=O at 1715, saturated ketone). Six equivalent protons as a singlet means two equivalent CH₃ groups attached to the carbonyl.

spectra.q: C₄H₈O₂: IR 1740 cm⁻¹, no O–H; ¹H NMR δ 1.25 (t, 3H), 2.05 (s, 3H), 4.12 (q, 2H). Identify the compound.
spectra.m: Ethyl acetate. DBE = 1; 1740 cm⁻¹ indicates ester C=O; ethyl on oxygen (OCH₂ at 4.12) and acetyl CH₃ singlet at 2.05.

spectra.q: C₇H₆O: IR 1700 cm⁻¹ and ~2720/2820 cm⁻¹; ¹H NMR δ 10.0 (s, 1H), 7.5–7.9 (m, 5H). Identify.
spectra.m: Benzaldehyde. DBE = 5 (ring + C=O). Aldehyde C–H pair of IR bands (Fermi doublet) and the 10.0 singlet confirm CHO; five aromatic H show a monosubstituted ring. C=O at ~1700 is lowered by conjugation.

spectra.q: An IR spectrum shows a strong broad band at 3350 cm⁻¹, no carbonyl band, and a strong band near 1050 cm⁻¹. What functional group is most consistent?
spectra.m: An alcohol (O–H stretch, hydrogen bonded, ~3350; C–O stretch ~1050, indicating a primary alcohol).

spectra.q: A mass spectrum shows M⁺ at m/z 156 and 158 in a 1:1 ratio and a base peak at m/z 77. Suggest a structural feature and a likely compound class.
spectra.m: The 1:1 M/M+2 pair indicates one bromine atom. m/z 77 is the phenyl cation C₆H₅⁺. M = 156 = C₆H₅ (77) + Br (79): bromobenzene.

spectra.q: A compound C₉H₁₂ shows ¹H NMR δ 1.25 (d, 6H), 2.90 (septet, 1H), 7.1–7.3 (m, 5H). Identify it.
spectra.m: Cumene (isopropylbenzene). DBE = 4 (benzene ring). The 6H doublet/1H septet pair is an isopropyl group on an aromatic ring (benzylic CH at 2.90).

spectra.q: A C₈H₁₀ compound shows only 3 ¹³C signals (δ ≈ 21, 129, 135) in the proton-decoupled spectrum. Propose a structure.
spectra.m: p-Xylene (1,4-dimethylbenzene): CH₃ (21 ppm), aromatic CH (129), and substituted aromatic C (135). The high symmetry gives just three signals.

spectra.q: C₅H₁₀O: IR 1715; ¹H NMR δ 0.95 (t, 3H), 1.60 (sextet, 2H), 2.14 (s, 3H), 2.40 (t, 2H). Identify and assign.
spectra.m: 2-Pentanone (CH₃COCH₂CH₂CH₃). DBE = 1 (ketone). δ 2.14 s = COCH₃; 2.40 t = COCH₂; 1.60 sextet = CH₂ coupled to CH₃ and CH₂; 0.95 t = terminal CH₃.

spectra.q: C₈H₈O₂: IR 1690 cm⁻¹ (strong), broad 2500–3300 cm⁻¹; ¹H NMR δ 2.35 (s, 3H), 7.25 (d, 2H), 7.95 (d, 2H), 12.0 (br s, 1H). Identify.
spectra.m: p-Toluic acid (4-methylbenzoic acid). DBE = 5 (ring + C=O). The very broad IR band and δ 12.0 are the carboxylic acid O–H; two aromatic doublets indicate para-substitution; methyl singlet at 2.35 is the aryl CH₃.
